test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 02 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the supreme law of India?
solution:
pThe correct answer is __**Indian Constitution**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Indian Constitution** is the **supreme law of India** because it establishes the framework that defines fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.

• All laws enacted by the **Parliament** or state legislatures, and all executive actions taken by the **President** or Governors, must be in conformity with the **Constitution**. If any law violates the provisions of the Constitution, the **Judiciary** has the power to declare it null and void.

• The **Supreme Court Judgment** is considered the law of the land under **Article 141**, but it is an interpretation of the law and the Constitution, not the supreme law itself. Judgments must align with constitutional mandates. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• The **Parliament** of India is the supreme legislative body, but its powers are derived from and limited by the **Constitution**. It cannot pass laws that override the **Basic Structure** of the Constitution as defined in the **Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• The **Indian Constitution** was adopted by the **Constituent Assembly** on **26 November 1949** and became effective on **26 January 1950**. It imparts **constitutional supremacy** rather than parliamentary supremacy. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

• A **President's Order** (such as an **Ordinance** under **Article 123**) has the same force as an Act of Parliament but is temporary and subject to the **Constitution** and judicial review. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Constitution of India** is the **longest written constitution** of any sovereign country in the world, originally containing **395 Articles** in **22 Parts** and **8 Schedules**.

• Currently, after various amendments, it has approximately **448 Articles** grouped into **25 Parts** and **12 Schedules**.

• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, the Chairman of the **Drafting Committee**, is widely regarded as the **Chief Architect** or the **Father of the Indian Constitution**.

• The **Preamble** of the Constitution declares India to be a **Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, and Democratic Republic**, ensuring justice, liberty, and equality to all its citizens.

• The **Constitution** was not printed but **calligraphed** in both **Hindi** and **English** by **Prem Behari Narain Raizada**.

• The **Constituent Assembly** took exactly **2 years, 11 months, and 18 days** to complete the final draft of the **Constitution**.

**Important Points__**

• **Article 13**: This article explicitly provides for the doctrine of **Judicial Review**. It states that all laws in force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of the Constitution, in so far as they are inconsistent with the provisions of **Fundamental Rights (Part III)**, shall be void.

• **Basic Structure Doctrine**: Established by the **Supreme Court** in **1973**, this doctrine prevents the **Parliament** from using its amendment powers under **Article 368** to alter the essential features of the **Constitution**, such as **Secularism**, **Federalism**, and **Democracy**.

• **Constitutional Supremacy vs. Parliamentary Supremacy**: Unlike the **United Kingdom**, where **Parliament** is supreme, India follows **Constitutional Supremacy**, where the **Constitution** is the highest legal authority.

• **Emergency Provisions**: Under **Articles 352, 356, and 360**, the **Constitution** provides for the suspension of certain rights and the shifting of the federal structure to a unitary one, yet even these actions must follow the **Constitutional** procedure.
